candidate_evidence.quote: RSC-1255 is an orally bioavailable, small-molecule direct pan-mutant and wild-type RAS inhibitor.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Malignancy has progressed on standard therapy

role_evidence.quote: RSC-1255 is administered orally twice daily, with and without food.

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: direct pan-mutant and wild-type RAS inhibitor

role_evidence.quote: RSC-1255 is administered orally twice daily alone or in combination with continuous hydroxychloroquine, with food.

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: direct pan-mutant and wild-type RAS inhibitor

role_evidence.quote: as monotherapy and in combination with the autophagy inhibitor hydroxychloroquine (HCQ)

flag.reason: HCQ is not a separately registered intervention and is optional in Phase 1b expansion; role as co-investigational agent vs add-on partner unclear.

source_quote.quote: Has either tissue agnostic tumors and documented RAS mutations or with glioblastoma with or without mutation in RAS

flag.reason: RAS mutation is required for non-glioblastoma tumours but not for glioblastoma; whether it counts as enrichment for the GBM cohort is unclear.

coder_notes: Single-arm basket trial. Hydroxychloroquine appears only in intervention/description text as an optional combination in Phase 1b; RSC-1255 coded as monotherapy since the arm states all participants receive RSC-1255 and primary outcomes are monotherapy MTD/RP2D. Glioblastoma enrols irrespective of RAS status. RSC-1255 listed once per registered intervention (escalation, expansion).
